column2: Data Poisoning in LLMs: Jailbreak-Tuning and Scaling Laws
column6: In-window (before 2026-07-09 cutoff). Fetched: empirical evaluation by FAR.AI (in-scope evaluator; authors Bowen, Murphy, Cai, Khachaturov, Gleave, Pelrine). Qualifying empirical model findings: across 24 frontier LLMs (1.5B-72B), larger models are significantly more susceptible to data poisoning, learning harmful behaviours from minimal poisoned data faster (a measured scaling law); GPT models remain vulnerable to poisoned fine-tuning despite moderation safeguards. Measured results about specific systems' safeguards -> qualifies. No matching report_id in canonical CSV (candidate miss).
